Laura — thanks for the clear MAP. Quick summary from our side and suggested next steps:

- Recommendation (initial pilot): Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) in eu-west for the first rollout. Rationale: predictable throughput for your concurrency, stronger tenant isolation, and we can provision with dedicated autoscaling policies to hit the 95th/50th latency targets.

- Fallback plan: Hosted (multi-tenant) with KV prefix caching and token-level privacy guards if procurement needs a faster signoff — this will have slightly higher variance but faster time-to-value.

- Private/on-prem: feasible but adds 6–10 weeks for network setup, KMS/HSM integration, and on-prem packaging. Recommend only if you require full air-gapped operation.

Action items from Redwood:
1) I'll share an "evaluation checklist" you can run against sample traffic (attached). This will give deterministic pass/fail on latency and throughput.
2) Karthik will follow up with a committed pricing window and delivery dates.
3) Monica will provide a short region latency benchmark and recommendations for eu-west node sizing.

We can support your 2026-07-21 pilot if hosting mode is locked by 2026-06-30 and procurement signs the SOW by 2026-07-12.

I've attached a slimmed eval_checklist.xlsx and a proposed cutover checklist. If that timeline works, we'll prepare the SOW draft for procurement review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min alignment call if helpful.

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference

Laura — added a short technical addendum focused on latency and data residency considerations. Highlights:

- Benchmarks (attached latency_bench_q1.csv): eu-west Dedicated with 2x A100-equivalent shows median token latency ~42ms and 95th ~150ms under your sample profile (prefix caching enabled).
- Cross-border backups: by default snapshots are stored in-region; we can enable encrypted backups to a customer-managed KMS in eu-west. That satisfies the data residency ask.
- Fallback mechanics: We'll pre-configure a Hosted fallback route with traffic-splitting and automatic KV cache priming so failover can occur within 20–30 minutes; the MAP will include the exact runbook steps.
